evidence: The mechanism is as described but the failure needs a tight race. The opt-out skip block (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:881-912) calls only _retract_stale_approvals_on_skip (tasks.py:483-517), which dismisses runs that already carry a posted_review_id at a head other than the payload head (logic/approvals.py:44-52); it never changes run status. _supersede_prior_runs (tasks.py:415-432) runs only on the main path (tasks.py:1054) and the receiver leg (tasks.py:1222), so a QUEUED/REVIEWING run for the PR keeps its Temporal workflow after the opt-out skip returns. Toggle-off does not supersede either: review_hog's settings serializer imports only has_reviewable_repo_config (products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:16,78) and the stamphog facade exports no supersede function (facade/api.py). The old run then reaches post_verdict with status still live: the SUPERSEDED guards (temporal/activities.py:666-672, 700-713, 776-793) are inert, and the only thing stopping it is the head guard (activities.py:673-684), which reads GitHub's current head and skips (marking SUPERSEDED, dismissing any orphan) when it differs from run.head_sha. That is what happens in the ordinary case, because every event that lands on this skip path with a live run is a synchronize that moved the head (reopened does not move it, and a same-head completion is the pre-opt-out run finishing, which the carve-out docstring at tasks.py:163-165 accepts). The residual failure is the TOCTOU between that get_pr at :673 and post_approve_review at :745 (with the superseded_now read at :700 and list_own_active_approvals at :738 in between): a push landing inside that window makes the skip-path retraction run before posted_review_id exists (persisted at :753-756), the run then posts an approval pinned to the old head (logic/github_client.py:986-997) and saves COMPLETED/APPROVED, and no newer run exists to sweep it. The tree treats this exact race shape as real for the supersession case and closes it with the terminal sweep (activities.py:560-588, tests/test_integration.py:618, 862); a skip path has no newer run so nothing sweeps until the next head-changing delivery, whose retraction (approvals.py:52 excludes only the new head) then dismisses it. Not must_fix: the pusher is the team's own agent on a bot-authored draft the team created, the window is a few GitHub round-trips, and the exposure self-heals on the next push. Not should_fix: the identical no-supersede shape is pre-existing on the label skip (tasks.py:949-951) and the author-below-write skip (tasks.py:981-983), so the PR extended an existing pattern to a new PR class rather than introducing it. It still earns a consider because the PR's own safety claim (tasks.py:163-165, 'safety is never preference-gated') covers only already-posted approvals, the design supersedes live runs for the analogous repo-disable and repo-removal opt-outs (presentation/views.py:242-253, tasks.py:679-695, whose docstring says a run already in the sandbox could still post a verdict), _retract_approvals_on_base_retarget already pairs supersede with dismiss right above (tasks.py:464-471), and the fix is one conditional update inside the existing try at :890-898 that routes the old run through the guards that already exist (:700-713 superseded_now, :776-793 lost-terminal-save orphan dismissal). The opt-out test (tests/test_tasks.py:796-827) mocks the dismissal and never asserts the live run's status, so it neither pins nor contradicts the behaviour.
notes: Would upgrade to should_fix if the window were wider than the post_verdict read-then-post span (for example if the head check ran before the sandbox instead of immediately before the GitHub write, or if GitHub did not auto-dismiss and the approval survived the next push, which it does not: approvals.py:52 retracts it on the next head-changing delivery), or if a live run could be created for a ready (non-draft) self-driving PR so the orphan satisfied branch protection at merge time. Would downgrade to not real if post_verdict re-read the head after post_approve_review and dismissed on mismatch, or if the review_hog toggle-off path superseded in-flight inbox runs the way repo disable does.
